title: Where the twenty-mule teams stopped
text: Mojave was the western end of the twenty-mule-team borax route from Death Valley. In the 1880s, teams hauled borax about 165 miles from Death Valley to the railroad at Mojave. The town began in 1876 as a construction camp on the Southern Pacific Railroad. It later served as headquarters for construction of the Los Angeles Aqueduct.

s1.title: Mojave, California
s1.quote: From 1884 to 1889, the town was the western terminus of the 166-mile (267 km), twenty-mule team at Harmony Borax Works in Death Valley. ... The town of Mojave began in 1876 as a construction camp on the Southern Pacific Railroad. ... later served as headquarters for construction of the Los Angeles Aqueduct.

s2.title: Harmony Borax Works
s2.quote: Coleman had unique borax wagons designed to get the product to the closest railhead in Mojave, California.

s3.title: Harmony Borax Works
s3.quote: Twenty-mule team wagons were once used to transport borax 165 miles from Death Valley to Mojave.
